hints: The numbers go up, then down, then up. Look at every other number.
Write the 1st, 3rd and 5th numbers as one series: 10, 9, 8.
The next number is the 7th, so it belongs to the series 10, 9, 8. That series goes down by 1 each time.

steps.action: Check the differences: 13 − 10 = 3, then 13 to 9 is a drop of 4, then 12 − 9 = 3, then 12 to 8 is a drop of 4. Up 3, down 4, taking turns.
steps.why: When the steps go up and down in turns, split the list into two series.

steps.action: Take the 1st, 3rd and 5th numbers: 10, 9, 8. The rule is −1.
Take the 2nd, 4th and 6th numbers: 13, 12, 11. The rule is also −1.
The blank is the 7th number, so it belongs to the first series: 8 − 1 = 7.
Check another way: the last step (8 to 11) was +3, so the next step is −4. 11 − 4 = 7. Same result. The answer is 7.

trapNotes.10: This is the next number of the second series (13, 12, 11). The 7th number belongs to the first series: 10, 9, 8.
trapNotes.14: This adds 3 again. The steps take turns: +3, −4, +3, −4. The last step was +3, so now take 4 away.
trapNotes.15: This adds 4. The step of 4 goes down, not up: 13 − 4 = 9 and 12 − 4 = 8.
